TESTIMONY OF DANIEL P. D'ALESSANDRO, DEPUTY TAX POLICY COUNSEL DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: Tuesday, January 28, 2025
LD 41 -- "Resolve, Authorizing the State Tax Assessor to Convey the Interest of the
State in Certain Real Estate in the Unorganizecl Territory"
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation
Committee -- good afternoon, my name is Daniel D'Alessandro, Deputy Tax Policy
Counsel in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am
testifying at the request of the Administration in Support of LD 41 "Resolve,
Authorizing the State Tax Assessor to Convey the Interest of the State in Certain Real Estate in the Unorganized Territory."
This is a department bill which is presented each year to allow the State Tax Assessor to sell properties that have been acquired by the State through the tax lien process. As you know, Maine Revenue Services serves as the local assessor for
properties located in the unorganized territory of the State. Title 36, Section 1283
of the Maine Revised Statutes requires the State Tax Assessor to report to the Legislature all property in the unorganized territory that has been tax-acquired by the State and, after authorization by the Legislature, to sell that property. This Resolve is a statutory step in that process. The properties listed in the Resolve were acquired by the State through the foreclosure of tax liens for nonpayment of property taxes. None of the properties included in this Resolve are occupied
homesteads.
This process is a routine element of unorganized territory tax administration,
and the administrative costs can be absorbed within the current UT budget. The
1

General Fund is reimbursed from the Unorganized Territory Education Services Fund for the costs of property tax administration in the unorganized territory.
The Administration looks forward to Working with the Committee on the
bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide
additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.

Testimony ofRep. Kristen Cloutier presenting
LD 41 Resolve, Authorizing the State Tax Assessor to Convey the Interest of the
State in Certain Real Estate in the Unorganized Territory
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation
Good afternoon Senator Grohoski and colleagues on the Taxation Committee. As you know, my name is Kristen Cloutier, and I represent House District 94, which includes part of my hometown of Lewiston. I am pleased to sponsor LD 41 Resolve, Authorizing the State Tax Assessor to
Convey the Interest of the State in Certain Real Estate in the Unorganized Territory on behalf of the Department of Administrative and Financial Services and Maine Revenue Services.
LD 4l is a resolve that follows the established process for addressing tax-acquired properties in
Maine's Unorganized Territory. It provides a structured and fair approach to handling properties with matured tax liens from 2022, while protecting both the state's interests and providing consideration for former property owners.
Thank you for your consideration. I will now defer to the department who can present the bill in more detail and answer any questions you may have.
